questions.prompt: Why does the club keep contacts in Constellation rather than in a spreadsheet someone owns?
questions.explanation: Because the member who built a sponsor relationship graduates, and the relationship shouldn't graduate with them. A shared record with history is what makes the relationship the club's rather than one person's.

answers.text: So the relationship and its history survive the member who built it
Because spreadsheets can't store email addresses reliably
So officers can see who has talked to whom for XP purposes
To satisfy a university records requirement

questions.prompt: What makes a good follow-up on a contact record?
questions.explanation: A date and an owner. "We should reach out sometime" is not a follow-up — nothing reminds anyone, and nobody is answerable for it.

answers.text: A specific date and a named person who owns it
A note saying the club should reach out soon
A high priority flag on the contact
A message drafted in the composer and left unsent

questions.explanation: It groups a set of contacts you're working through together so you can see coverage — who's been contacted, who replied, and who has been sitting untouched for weeks.

answers.text: Grouping contacts you're working through together, so you can see coverage
Sending one message to every contact in the database at once
Tracking how much money each sponsor has given

questions.prompt: The composer drafts a message to a sponsor for you. What should you do before sending?
questions.explanation: Read it and edit it. Drafting tools are assistive — a sponsor can tell when nobody looked at what they were sent, and that costs the club far more than the minutes it saved.

answers.text: Read it properly and edit it before it goes anywhere
Send it as-is — it uses the club's brand voice
Forward it to an officer to send on your behalf
Run it through the composer a second time

questions.prompt: Constellation will remind you about overdue follow-ups without you checking the CRM.
questions.explanation: True. A weekday-morning Slack DM lists what has slipped. That nudge is the difference between a CRM and a list of good intentions nobody reopens.
